ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: An ant crawls carefully around the edges of a cube, starting at point $P$ and in the direction of the arrow. At the end of the first edge he chooses to go either left or right. He then turns the other way at the end of the next edge and continues like this, turning right or left alternately at the end of each successive edge. After how many edges does the ant return to point $P$ for the first time? <image1>

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a cube drawn in perspective, point P is marked near the upper front right corner, and an arrow from P along the adjacent upper right side edge points toward the rear upper right direction, determining the first edge on which the ant starts to walk. Reasoning: Regard the cube as a graph composed of 8 vertices and 12 edges. The ant first walks from P along the arrow to the adjacent vertex; after arriving, it cannot go backward, and can only choose left or right among the other two edges, and afterward each time it reaches a vertex it alternately turns left and right. Because the cube is symmetric, choosing left or choosing right the first time will only obtain mirror-image paths, with the same return length. Tracing along one of the choices: from P along the arrow to the rear upper right vertex, then turn to the rear upper left vertex, then turn in the opposite direction to the rear lower left vertex, then turn to the front lower left vertex, then turn to the front lower right vertex, and finally turn back to P. This exactly passes through 6 edges. Along the way, the endpoints of the first 5 edges are not P, so the first time returning to P is after finishing walking the 6th edge.

After how many edges does the ant return to point $P$ for the first time?

method.method_draft: Image: the cube is shown in perspective, with point P marked at the upper front-right corner and an arrow fixing the initial direction along the adjacent top edge. Text: after that first edge, the ant must alternate left and right turns at each vertex. Bridge: model the cube as its edge graph and follow the forced cycle determined by the marked start and alternating-turn rule. On a cube, that rule carries the ant around one 6-edge loop on the surface before the starting corner can be reached again; any shorter return would repeat a vertex/edge pattern too early and would violate the alternation. So the first return to P is after 6 edges.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个透视画出的立方体，点 P 标在上前右角附近，箭头从 P 沿着相邻的上方右侧边指向后上右方向，确定了蚂蚁开始走的第一条棱。
推理：把立方体看作由 8 个顶点和 12 条棱组成的图。蚂蚁从 P 先沿箭头走到相邻顶点；到达后不能倒退，只能在另外两条棱中选左或右，以后每到一个顶点就左右交替转向。由于立方体对称，第一次选左或选右只会得到镜像路径，返回长度相同。沿其中一种选择追踪：从 P 沿箭头到后上右顶点，然后转到后上左顶点，再按相反方向转到后下左顶点，再转到前下左顶点，再转到前下右顶点，最后转回 P。这正好经过 6 条棱。途中前 5 条棱的终点都不是 P，因此第一次回到 P 是走完第 6 条棱后。
